gaps.sentence: You ___ take an umbrella — the forecast says heavy rain all day.
gaps.explanation: 'Should' recommends a sensible action: should take.

gaps.sentence: We ___ have taken the wrong turning — the signpost was knocked down in the storm.
gaps.explanation: 'May have + participle' offers one possible explanation of a past event.

gaps.sentence: ___ we take the motorway, or will the coast road be quicker?
gaps.explanation: 'Should we ...?' asks for advice or an opinion: Should.

gaps.sentence: That ___ be Sarah at the door — she is in Berlin until Friday.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' expresses logical impossibility: can't be Sarah.

gaps.sentence: There ___ be a supervisor present when students use the lab.
In this lab, food and drink ___ be brought past the reception area.
gaps.explanation: Written prohibitions use 'must not': must not be brought.

gaps.sentence: He ___ have missed the train — he left home two hours early.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have' expresses near-certainty that something did not happen: can't have missed.

gaps.sentence: This bill ___ be right — we only ordered two coffees.
gaps.hint: an obvious mistake, so it is impossible
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' shows the speaker believes something is not possible: can't be right.
